name: Nd:YAG laser hair removal

lead: Nd:YAG is the hair-removal laser used for darker skin tones, reducing facial and body hair while limiting absorption in the surface melanin. Wikipedia lists the 1064 nm wavelength as the one for dark skin, and a 2022 prospective study said alexandrite and Nd:YAG are the most effective options in lighter and darker skin phototypes respectively.

The longer wavelength is absorbed less by skin pigment and penetrates deeper, so it heats hair-follicle melanin while sparing the surface better. Studies of fluence and histology in the early 2000s examined millisecond Nd:YAG lasers for hair removal.

paras: It is done in a clinic over repeated sessions spaced weeks apart, since lasers act on actively growing follicles. Fine or light hair usually needs more sessions. Some clinics use an "in motion" technique, which a 2022 study compared with the traditional approach.

Redness, swelling, pain, burns and pigment change are possible, as with other laser hair removal. Results are a reduction rather than guaranteed removal. The 1064 nm beam is invisible, so eye protection is used.

chain: Follicles heated with less surface absorption
angle.text: The 1064 nm wavelength penetrates deeper and is absorbed less by surface pigment, so follicles are heated with less skin damage and hair is reduced on darker skin. It is the option people with darker skin tones turn to for facial and body hair.

lead: Nd:YAG laser hair removal uses a 1064 nm neodymium-doped yttrium aluminium garnet laser to reduce dark hair. Wikipedia lists it as the hair-removal laser for dark skin. [1]
Bell Laboratories first demonstrated Nd:YAG laser operation in 1964, and the laser is used in cosmetic medicine for hair removal and minor vascular defects. [2]
Published studies include fluence comparisons and histology from 2001 and a 2022 prospective study comparing traditional and "in motion" Nd:YAG techniques. [3][4][5]

paras: A 2023 study measured hair temperature changes under alexandrite and Nd:YAG hair-removal lasers to understand the photothermal process. [6]

Wikipedia states that Nd:YAG can treat black hair in people with darker skin with some success. [1] A 2022 prospective study of 40 patients (skin types 2 to 6) compared traditional and in-motion Nd:YAG hair removal. [4] A 2001 study of 15 subjects compared fluences of 50, 80 and 100 J/cm2. [3]
General risks of laser hair removal include redness, swelling, acne flares, discoloration, burns and infection. [1]

Human studies include the fluence comparison [3], histologic evaluation of a millisecond Nd:YAG laser in six patients [5], and the in-motion comparison [4]. Registered trials examine laser hair removal for pilonidal disease and hidradenitis suppurativa. [7][8]
